diagnosis: The best code is not a jammed optimum: only one pair attains the maximum within $10^{-9}$, only two points have any contact, and 254 points are rattlers. Yet roughly 1400 pairs lie within $10^{-4}$ of the maximum, mostly within $5\times10^{-7}$, so it is an unequalized near-contact plateau rather than a KKT-stationary, rigid configuration. Gradients and LP steps are dominated by the single worst pair, whose force cannot balance independently on each point, so each improvement merely promotes another nearly tied pair and progress decays to about $3\times10^{-5}$ total. Starting every search from this incumbent and applying Adam plus local LP therefore returns to the same basin; the missing structure is a spanning, balanced contact graph in which essentially every point is pinned by at least five contacts on $S^5$ and many contacts are exactly tied.

diagnosis: The best code is highly degenerate: at the $10^{-9}$ contact threshold the maximum is attained by essentially one pair, with 252 of 256 points being rattlers and no spanning contact graph. Behind that pair sits a wall of roughly 1,400 pairs only about $2\times10^{-8}$ below the maximum, so moving the bottleneck pair immediately loads the plateau. This explains the stalled progress: Adam/LP polishing can repeatedly shave the isolated pair against the plateau, but only by the plateau gap, yielding the observed diminishing gain of just $3.3\times10^{-5}$ in 47 programs within the record's basin. The missing structural property is a balanced, rigid, nearly isostatic contact network — many pairs exactly tied at the maximum, most points carrying several contacts, and contact normals spanning each point's tangent space — rather than a single bottleneck pair floating above an almost-tied plateau.

diagnosis: The image shows only two pairs exactly at the maximum: four points have one contact at the $10^{-9}$ threshold and 252 are rattlers, so the incumbent is not jammed or positively stressed. Crucially, however, roughly 1,300–1,400 pairs sit only about $2\times10^{-8}$ below the maximum—a near-active wall comparable to the $256\cdot5-15=1265$ rotationally reduced degrees of freedom—so reducing the top pair soon collides with that entire plateau. This explains why 63 largely record-inherited LSE/Riesz/LP programs have gained only $3.3\times10^{-5}$ in total: local polishing can shave the current top pairs but cannot make the collective rearrangement needed to lower the wall. The missing property is an exactly equalized, spanning contact graph, averaging roughly $2(1265)/256\approx9.9$ contacts per point, with nonnegative equilibrium stresses on its active pairs rather than load concentrated on two pairs in an otherwise unstructured configuration.
